answer:
In the picture, crowds of villagers line the riverbank and the bridge, cheering loudly as several dragon boats race forward. Watching the exciting scene, an elderly couple smile happily, and the woman says, "How wonderful! The dragon boat race in our village is getting more and more lively!"

The picture vividly shows that traditional festivals and folk activities are flourishing in China's countryside. This revival is significant in several ways. First, it enriches villagers' cultural life and brings people together, strengthening the bonds within the community. Second, such events help pass on traditional culture to younger generations, so that customs like dragon boat racing will not fade away. Third, they attract tourists and promote local economies, contributing to rural revitalization.

In my view, we should spare no effort to support this trend. Local governments can invest in facilities and organize cultural events, while young people should take an active part in them instead of regarding them as old-fashioned. Only when traditions are truly alive in daily life can our culture remain vigorous.
